passages.quote: ## It's Scholarship Time!
**One Application, Mutiple Scholarships.**

**Bridging the Gap Scholarship**

$1,000 for one or more recipients.  Must complete the Reach Higher Montana Scholarship application, and will or have aged out of the Foster Care system.

**Agri Industries**

Amounts vary. High School Senior or College student interested in a career related to irrigation, electrical trades, HVAC, Water wells (pumps/drilling), underground utilities, plumbing, welding, or fabrication.

**AMTOPP Scholarship**

(1) $500 scholarship. HS Senior, 2.0 GPA or higher, member of FFA.

01. When can I apply for scholarships using the “It’s Scholarship Time” application?
    - The “It’s Scholarship Time” application is open annually from January 1 thru March 1.

06. Can I submit a paper application?
    - No, we are only able to accept applications through our online scholarship program.

07. Will I have to complete separate applications for each scholarship I am eligible to apply for?
    - Yes and no. Individual scholarships will have supplemental questions that you will need to complete before you can submit each application. Because some scholarships use the same questions, you will only have to answer the question once and that answer will show up on any scholarships that use that same question. You will only have to complete the eligibility questions once per scholarship year to determine which scholarships you are eligible to apply for.

09. Do I have to submit an ‘official’ transcript for proof of grades/GPA?
    - No, we will accept unofficial transcripts as long as the date the report was pulled, your


       name, student ID number, and GPA are visible.

12. Can I reapply for a scholarship?
    - Yes! All of the scholarships available through the “It’s Scholarship Time” application are non-renewable meaning they are awarded on a year by year basis only. Applicants are encouraged to reapply each year if they remain eligible for the application whether or not they have previously won the scholarship. Every year, applicants must complete an application for any scholarships which they are eligible for and will be re-evaluated with the current year applications.

13. If I have previously won a scholarship and then reapply, am I more likely to receive it again?
    - No. Every year an application is open, a new committee will evaluate submissions. They do not receive applicant names or information on any prior awards won. This ensures everyone has an equal opportunity each year they apply.

14. How will I receive scholarship funds I am selected to receive?
    - All scholarship awards will be paid directly to the school you will be attending. You will receive an email with follow-up instructions that you must complete before funds will be sent; these include provision of your final prior semester grades or transcript and an enrollment verification form that your school will have to complete on your behalf.

15. How will my award be paid out?
    - All scholarship awards are sent to your school for the full amount, the first term you are enrolled. Be aware, however, that each post-secondary institution reserves the right to determine how your award is applied to your student account. It is standard practice for schools to split the total award amount equally across two semesters or three trimesters depending on academic schedules.

16. When is my scholarship awarded?
    - This depends on how quickly you, the applicant, return the required follow-up documents that will be requested from you. Once your grades and your enrollment verification are received, funds will be disbursed within two weeks.
    - Because checks are mailed, we cannot guarantee how long it will take for your funds to appear on your student account. Total time is dependent on many factors including the US Postal Service, how campus mail is handled, how big the financial aid staff is, how busy they are, and more. Remember, the sooner you complete your follow-up tasks, the sooner we can release your funds.

19. Can I still submit an application if I missed the deadline?
    - No. We have set a firm deadline of March 1st at 11:59 PM MST. Applicants are encouraged to apply early so that they have time to complete the application on time.

### AMTOPP FFA Scholarship

The Association of Montana Turf, Ornamental & Pest Professionals (AMTOPP) was founded in 1990. AMTOPP promotes high standards and ethics within the turf, ornamental and application pesticide industry. AMTOPP provides professional greens industry education and training for our members and the Montana community. AMTOPP works with legislative and regulatory bodies on matters concerning the turf, ornamental and pesticide application industry.

The Association of Montana Turf, Ornamental, and Pest Professionals will award a $500 scholarship annually through Montana FFA.

# College Scholarship Guidelines

## <u>Purpose.</u>

Montana FFA members represent all sectors of business, from agriculture to nursing to engineering. The Montana FFA Foundation provides funding for students to attain a technical or higher education degree so that they can continue to create an educated, vibrant workforce of FFA Alumni in our state.

## <u>Who can apply.</u>

Any Montana FFA member who is a high school senior or college freshman and meets the following criteria may apply for the Foundation College Scholarships: Active FFA member Two (2) years of Ag Ed courses completed

2.0 GPA
## <u>Application timeline.</u>

Students apply in the fall and are awarded scholarships in the spring to be used the following fall for college. A link to the online application will be posted on the Montana FFA website when the application opens: montanaffa.org > Applications> College Scholarship Application [http://montanaffa.org/applications/](http://montanaffa.org/applications/)

## <u>Application materials.</u>

Students who apply must upload a photo of themselves and their transcript to their online application. They must also have their advisor and a community member complete the Scholarship Reference Form by the December 31st deadline in order to have a complete application. Students are responsible for making sure references receive the email link and are completed by the deadline. <u>Additional Materials needed for a</u> <u>complete application:</u> Headshot of the student School transcript Reference form (advisor) by the December 31st Reference form (community member) by the December 31st

## <u>Recipient correspondence.</u>

Students must submit a thank-you to the Montana FFA Foundation immediately following the award notification as well as proof of college enrollment and a copy of their classes upon enrollment (see application timeline). You will be notified on whom to address the thank-you card and will need to mail it to the Montana FFA Foundation. <u>Complete verification materials</u>:

[provider postal address omitted; thank-you card required]

passages.quote: # College Scholarship Review Rubric

**DIRECTIONS.** The scholarship selection committee will score each section individually. Sections are scored on a scale
from one (1) to five (5) based upon criteria outlined in each section. This scale represents the raw points available.
The raw score is then multiplied by a weighted number, which varies in each section, to produce the total score
for the section (**bolded** box at bottom of far-right column). The total scores from each section are then summed to produce
an overall total score for the application. The total score for the application is not necessarily revealing of the final ranking
of the applicant as compared to the scores of other applications. The purpose of assigning a score is to provide an
indicator so that the selection committee may consider special circumstances and adjust the final rankings as needed.
**_10 points possible_** – **Cumulative high school GPA on a 4.0 scale. Size of class, and rank in class.**

## Future Farmers of America (FFA)

[Apply Now\\
\\
(opens in a new tab)](https://montanaffa.org/applications/)

- This program is open to seniors graduating from high schools in Montana and graduates of those high schools who are enrolled as freshmen at a college or vocational school in any state and planning to major in a field related to the horticultural or arboriculture  industry.
- Applicants must be members of FFA and have completed at least 2 years of agricultural education classes.
- They must have a GPA of 2.0 or higher.
- Selection is based on academic achievement (10 points); FFA leadership, including agricultural education courses completed (15 points); an essay describing their career objectives and why they have selected a career or vocation in agriculture (15 points); their FFA Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE) project (20 points); an essay on their community service and their role in those activities (10 points); financial need (5 points); a letter of reference from their adviser (5 points), and a letter of reference from a community member (5 points).

[image omitted]

## 4H

- Purpose: The 4-H Scholarship, established by AMTOPP in 2012, supports Montana 4-H members (ages 9-19) in beautification projects involving landscape or arboriculture, fostering interest and skills in the 'greens industry.'
- Eligible Projects: Funded projects may include starting a community garden, installing native gardens in local parks, planting trees to combat invasive species, or creating a spirit garden.
- Eligibility Requirements: Applicants must be current Montana 4-H members and between the ages of 9 and 19.
- Application Deadline: March 13, 2026
